CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Academic & Competitive Programs
Research Area — Clubs that compete regionally and nationally
Speech & Debate is the flagship by a wide margin — a top-20 NSDA program with charter and 200 Club status. Model UN,
Science Olympiad (Div B & C), World Quest, and the Math Team round out the competitive slate. Mock trial, decathlon,
and business chapters are not evident.
AT A GLANCE
Flagship Speech & Debate — NSDA top-20 program nationally (Schools of Excellence),
NSDA charter and 200 Club status.
Model UN Competes at local and international conferences, including NAIMUN at
Georgetown.
Science Olympiad Division B (MS) and Division C (US); reached the NC state tournament in
2026.
World Quest Academic current-affairs competition; the team faces local high schools
annually.
Math Math Club / CLS Math Team competes interscholastically.
Individual STEM A Latin junior placed at the NC State Science & Engineering Fair in spring
2026.
Clubs That Compete
This dossier covers the non-sport, non-arts clubs that engage in interscholastic competition — the segment
where claims can be cross-checked against external governing bodies rather than relying on the School's own
description. Charlotte Latin's competitive footprint is led, by a wide margin, by Speech & Debate.
Speech & Debate — The Flagship
Charlotte Latin's Speech & Debate program is a genuine national-tier operation, and the supporting evidence is
external and specific. The team earned the NSDA Debate Schools of Excellence Award, placing it among the
top 20 debate programs in the country. It holds charter status in the National Speech & Debate Association
— the association's highest team honor, based on participation relative to enrollment — and in 2025 earned
membership in the NSDA's 200 Club. Program director Bilal Butt has received a second NSDA Diamond award,
with his teams accumulating more than 30,000 NSDA points over a decade of coaching. [Sources:
charlottelatin.org — News & Speech and Debate; NSDA]
Recent national-tournament results
Students Event Result
Anisha Chandra & Divija Rao Public Forum Debate 5th at the NSDA National Tournament
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Students Event Result
Natalie Berman & Nicholas Willett Public Forum Debate 25th at the NSDA National Tournament
Isabel Yang World Schools Debate 33rd at the NSDA National Tournament
Alaric Pan ('23) Academic All-American NSDA Academic All-American (top ~1%
of members)
Sources: charlottelatin.org news ('Charlotte Latin Places in Top 20 Debate Programs'; 'Speech & Debate All-American'). The program
spans both Middle and Upper School.
Model United Nations
Model UN delegates research global issues and represent assigned nations at local and international
conferences. The School highlights participation in the North American Invitational Model UN (NAIMUN) at
Georgetown University, and notes that the Model UN and Debate programs have undertaken international travel.
Specific delegate-award tallies are not consistently published year to year, so this entry is reported at the
program level rather than with a medal count. [Sources: charlottelatin.org — Clubs; Upper School Profile]
Science Olympiad
Charlotte Latin fields Science Olympiad teams in Division B (Middle School) and Division C (Upper School).
Science Olympiad is a team STEM competition of roughly 23 events spanning biology, earth science, chemistry,
physics, and engineering, advancing from regional to state to national tournaments. Charlotte Latin's Division C
team appears in the field for the 2026 North Carolina State Tournament, indicating it advanced out of the
regional round that season. A specific state placement is not asserted here, because the public result table lists
participating schools without a confirmed finishing rank for Latin. [Sources: NC Science Olympiad; Duosmium
2026 NC State (Div. C)]
Verification note: reaching the state tournament is confirmable; an exact placement is not, so none is claimed.
World Quest
World Quest prepares students for global citizenship through current affairs, geography, and history, and the
School states that its team competes annually against local high schools. This is an academic-quiz-style
competition distinct from Model UN. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
Mathematics
The Math Club introduces members to interscholastic mathematics competition through the CLS Math Team,
and the separate CLS Math Tutors club extends math engagement into service via tutoring partnerships with
local schools. Competition-level results are not published in detail, so this is reported as an active competitive
offering rather than with specific standings. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
Individual Academic Competition
Beyond team clubs, Charlotte Latin students compete individually in STEM. In spring 2026 the School reported
that a Latin junior placed at the North Carolina State Science & Engineering Fair. Individual science-fair and
research competition is a recurring feature of the School's news. [Source: charlottelatin.org — School News, April
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
2026]
What Is Not Evident
For completeness and to avoid overstating the competitive slate: the School's published club roster does not
show a Mock Trial team, an Academic Decathlon team, a DECA/FBLA/BPA business chapter, or a
CyberPatriot/cybersecurity team. Robotics is present primarily at the Middle School level; a competition circuit
affiliation (FIRST or VEX) is not confirmed in the School's own materials and is therefore not claimed here.
Absence from public materials is not proof of non-existence, but these are not asserted without a source.
Source List
1. Charlotte Latin School — News: 'Charlotte Latin Places in Top 20 Debate Programs in U.S.A.'
2. Charlotte Latin School — Speech and Debate program page; 'Speech & Debate All-American' news.
3. National Speech & Debate Association — Schools of Excellence, charter status, 200 Club, Diamond awards.
4. Charlotte Latin School — Student Clubs / Clubs (Model UN, World Quest, Math Club).
5. NC Science Olympiad (ncscienceolympiad.ncsu.edu) and Duosmium 2026 NC State Tournament, Division C.
6. Charlotte Latin School — School News (NC State Science & Engineering Fair, April 2026).
7. Charlotte Latin School — Upper School Profile (Model UN/Debate international travel).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 3

CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Club Catalog & Descriptions
Research Area — Non-sport, non-arts clubs and activities, TK–12
25 in-scope Upper School clubs, a 25+ rotating Middle School model, and enrichment-based Lower School programming.
Speech & debate feeders, Model UN, Science Olympiad, and a deep service slate stand out; arts clubs are listed
separately for a clean count.
AT A GLANCE
Upper School (in 25 distinct clubs/organizations outside sports and the arts, drawn from the
scope) School's published Upper School club list.
Middle School Students choose from 25+ rotating offerings, meeting weekly in 8–10 week
cycles (30-minute sessions) so they sample several over a year. [Source:
charlottelatin.org]
Lower School (TK–5) Club life is delivered mainly through after-school enrichment (Hawks' Club)
rather than a named student-club roster — flagged as a structural difference,
not a data gap.
Excluded as arts 5 Upper School clubs (a cappella, improv, thespian society, literary journal,
creative writing) are listed in the closing transparency note.
Count method Upper School: 27 published clubs minus 5 arts/arts-adjacent, plus 3 service
organizations named in the page's 'special notes' = 25 in scope.
Scope & Methodology
This dossier catalogs Charlotte Latin School student clubs and activities that fall outside of athletics and the
arts. Performing- and literary-arts clubs (a cappella, improv, theater honor societies, the literary journal, and the
creative-writing club) are listed separately in a transparency note at the end rather than silently dropped, so the
count is auditable. The Upper School roster is drawn directly from the School's published club list; the Middle
School and Lower School sections reflect what the School publishes about those divisions, which is structural
rather than a full named roster. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Student Life / Clubs]
Grade-band convention: Upper School clubs serve grades 9–12; Middle School clubs serve grades 6–8
(Charlotte Latin's Middle School); Lower School covers TK–grade 5. Where the School specifies a narrower
range, that range is used; where it does not, the division is tagged and the absence of a published grade range is
noted rather than inferred.
Upper School Club Roster (Grades 9–12)
The table below enumerates every in-scope Upper School club with a short purpose statement (paraphrased
from the School's descriptions) and a thematic category used consistently across this dossier package. [Source:
charlottelatin.org — Student Clubs / Clubs]

Source: Charlotte Latin School, Student Clubs — Clubs page (charlottelatin.org/student-life/student-clubs/clubs). Descriptions
paraphrased.
Middle School Clubs (Grades 6–8)
Middle School runs on a rotating sampler model: students choose from more than 25 offerings, meet once a
week for an 8–10 week cycle in 30-minute sessions, then rotate to a different club. The design is deliberately
exposure-oriented — the goal is breadth rather than a single-season commitment. Volunteers and faculty advise
the sessions. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
The School names five of the more popular Middle School offerings: Cooking Club, Just Dance Club, Robotics
Club, Student Council, and Sports Club. Two of these touch the arts/sports boundary (Just Dance leans
toward dance; Sports Club toward athletics); they are reported here because the School lists them as general
Middle School clubs, with the boundary noted. In addition, the Middle School fields competitive academic teams
that are in clear scope — Science Olympiad (Division B) and a Middle School Speech & Debate offering for
7th and 8th graders. [Sources: charlottelatin.org; NC Science Olympiad]
Gap flagged honestly: Charlotte Latin does not publish a complete named Middle School club roster (the model rotates term to term), so
a full enumeration comparable to the Upper School list is not publicly available. The 25+ figure and the named examples are the School's
own.
Lower School (TK–Grade 5)
At the Lower School level, structured 'clubs' in the Upper/Middle sense are limited. Out-of-classroom
programming is delivered chiefly through Hawks' Club after-school care (TK–grade 5) and Enrichment
Programs, which are enrichment blocks rather than student-led clubs. This is a structural feature of the division,
not a missing-data problem. Notably, Lower School students have still produced standout extracurricular initiative
— a group was featured by Nickelodeon in December 2025 for founding a charity. [Sources: charlottelatin.org —
After School; School News]
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 3
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Transparency Note — Clubs Excluded as Arts / Arts-Adjacent
Per the series scope (outside sports and the arts), the following five published Upper School clubs are excluded
from the in-scope count and recorded here so the catalog is fully auditable:
• A cappella Club — informal vocal-music ensemble (performing art).
• Improv Club — improvisational theater (performing art).
• International Thespian Society — theater honor society, part of the Educational Theatre Association
(performing art).
• The Blue Review — the School's literary journal (creative writing / literary art).
• Creative Writing Club — creative-writing workshops, readings, and publication (creative writing / literary art).
Yearbook Club is retained in scope as a publication/journalism activity, consistent with the series rule that journalism and yearbook are in
scope while visual, performing, and literary arts are not.
Source List
1. Charlotte Latin School — Student Clubs / Clubs (charlottelatin.org/student-life/student-clubs/clubs).
2. Charlotte Latin School — After School: Hawks' Club & Enrichment Programs (charlottelatin.org/after-school).
3. Charlotte Latin School — School News (Lower School charity featured by Nickelodeon, Dec. 2025).
4. North Carolina Science Olympiad — Charlotte/State tournament listings (ncscienceolympiad.ncsu.edu; duosmium.org).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 4

sections.text:
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Governance, Formation, Funding & Discovery
Research Area — How clubs are run, started, funded, and found
Clubs are advisor-anchored and meet during the school day; students are encouraged to form their own with a faculty
advisor. Funding process and a named club fair are not publicly documented — reported here as honest gaps, with the
Middle School rotation serving as the discovery engine.
AT A GLANCE
Who runs clubs Faculty and volunteers advise; the Upper School supports student-formed
clubs.
Meeting time Built into the school day — Middle School club periods and an Upper School
activity/club period — not solely after school.
Formation Students may suggest and form clubs; a faculty advisor is the consistent
requirement.
Funding No public club-budget process; survey sentiment is positive (82% on 17
responses). Flagged as a gap.
Discovery Middle School rotation exposes students to many clubs by design; a named
all-School club fair is not confirmed. Flagged as a gap.
Why These Three Are Combined
This dossier merges three operational questions — how clubs are governed and formed, how they are funded,
and how students discover them. They are combined because Charlotte Latin publishes solid information on
governance and formation but relatively little on club budgets and on a formal discovery event; rather than ship
two thin documents, the funding and discovery material is folded in here with its gaps clearly marked.
Governance & Advising
Charlotte Latin clubs operate under faculty and volunteer guidance. In the Middle School, volunteers and faculty
advise the weekly 30-minute club sessions. In the Upper School, clubs enrich student life across service, global
studies, and leadership, and the School — corroborated by third-party reviews — is described as supportive of
student-led clubs. The consistent structural requirement across divisions is that a club has a faculty advisor.
[Sources: charlottelatin.org — Clubs; Niche]
Two governance bodies sit above the individual clubs. The elected Student Council plans events and channels
student concerns to administration, and the Honor Council (supported by its Advisory Board) administers the
Honor Code. Together they give the club ecosystem an elected student-government layer. [Source:
charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
Forming a New Club — How Hard Is It?
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
The published picture is encouraging but not fully specified. The School indicates that students can suggest and
form their own clubs, and most student-formed Upper School clubs meet during designated time in the
school-day schedule — a meaningful lowering of the barrier, since a new club does not have to compete with
after-school commitments for members. The reliably documented requirement is securing a faculty advisor.
[Sources: charlottelatin.org — Clubs; Niche review noting support for student-led clubs]
Gap flagged: Charlotte Latin does not publish a step-by-step new-club approval process (forms, sponsoring office, minimum
membership, or charter timeline). The 'faculty advisor required' rule is documented; the rest of the procedure is not public and is not
invented here.
Funding & Budget Process
This is the thinnest area in the entire package. Charlotte Latin does not publish a club budget process, per-club
allocations, or a student-government funding mechanism for non-sport, non-arts clubs. The only available signal
is third-party sentiment: on Niche, 82% of respondents agreed clubs get the funding they need — but from
just 17 self-selected responses, which is directional at best. Separately, the parent-run Latin Arts Association
funds arts programs (including a Friends of Speech & Debate branch that provides volunteer and hospitality
support to that team), but that is an arts-booster structure and out of scope for general club funding. [Sources:
Niche; charlottelatin.org — Latin Arts Association]
Honest position: no club funding figures or budget process are asserted. The 82% sentiment is reported only with its small-sample limit; it
is not a statement about actual budgets.
Discovery & Access
How do students find clubs? The strongest mechanism is structural. The Middle School rotation model —
sampling a new club every 8–10 weeks — is itself a discovery engine: over a year, a student is exposed to
several clubs without having to seek them out. In the Upper School, the in-school-day club period and the
published club list (plus the Veracross / MyLatin student portal) are the visible access points. [Sources:
charlottelatin.org — Clubs; MyLatin portal]
What is not confirmed is a named, all-School club fair or showcase event. Many schools run an activities fair at
the start of the year; Charlotte Latin's public materials do not document one by name. It may exist internally (often
surfaced only through the parent/student portal), but it is not claimed here without a source. [Gap flagged]
Gap flagged: a formal club-fair/showcase event is neither confirmed nor denied by public sources. The Middle School rotation is the
documented discovery mechanism; an Upper School fair is not.
Operational Summary
Charlotte Latin's club operations are advisor-anchored and schedule-supported: clubs meet during the school
day, a faculty advisor is the gateway, and students are encouraged to start their own. The system is clearly
functional and well-regarded, but the back-office specifics — exact formation procedure, club budgets, and a
named discovery event — are not published, and this dossier reports those as gaps rather than filling them with
assumption.
Source List
1. Charlotte Latin School — Student Clubs / Clubs (advising; student-formed clubs; school-day meeting time; StuCo; Honor Council).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
2. Niche — Charlotte Latin School (clubs support and funding sentiment; 17 responses; accessed June 2026).
3. Charlotte Latin School — Latin Arts Association (arts-booster funding structure; Friends of Speech & Debate).
4. Charlotte Latin School — MyLatin / Veracross student portal (access point for club information).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 3

sections.text:
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Participation & Popularity
Research Area — How many students take part, and which clubs lead
No hard non-sport club participation rate is published; the honest read combines a near-universal Middle School rotation
model, in-school-day Upper School club periods, and small-sample survey sentiment (94% positive on 17 responses).
Most-popular lists are the School's where stated.
AT A GLANCE
Hard club Not published by the School for non-sport/non-arts clubs — reported as a gap,
participation % not estimated.
Athletics benchmark ~90% of students play at least one sanctioned sport (grades 7–12) — a
separate, sports-only figure included only for context. [Source: Wikipedia/CLS]
Survey sentiment On Niche, 94% of respondents agreed there are plenty of clubs and 94%
agreed many students participate — but from only 17 self-selected responses.
Most-popular (MS) Cooking, Just Dance, Robotics, Student Council, and Sports Club, per the
School.
Most-popular (US) By external profile, Speech & Debate, Model UN, and the service slate are the
highest-visibility programs; the School does not rank Upper School clubs by
membership.
What the Data Does — and Doesn't — Show
Charlotte Latin does not publish a hard participation rate for non-sport, non-arts clubs. This is the thinnest
segment in the package, and the honest position is to report the proxies that exist, label their limits, and avoid
manufacturing a percentage. Three kinds of signal are available: the School's own statement of which clubs are
most popular, third-party survey sentiment, and structural facts about how the schedule pushes participation.
Structural Participation (the Strongest Evidence)
The clearest participation signal is structural rather than numerical. In the Middle School, club time is built into
the weekly schedule and every student selects a club each 8–10 week cycle, so Middle School club participation
is effectively near-universal by design — students rotate through several clubs across a year. In the Upper
School, clubs meet during designated periods in the school day, lowering the barrier to joining relative to schools
where everything is after-school. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs; Return-to-Campus schedule notes]
Most-Popular Clubs
Middle School — named by the School
Charlotte Latin explicitly identifies its more popular Middle School offerings as Cooking Club, Just Dance Club,
Robotics Club, Student Council, and Sports Club. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Upper School — by external profile (not a School ranking)
Charlotte Latin does not publish an Upper School club popularity ranking. Judged by external footprint — national
results, news coverage, and program scale — the highest-profile non-sport/non-arts programs are Speech &
Debate (a top-20 national program), Model United Nations, Science Olympiad, and the Service Council slate
that culminates in the Service Society. This is an inference about visibility, not a membership count, and is
labeled as such.
Third-Party Survey Sentiment
The school-review site Niche reports that, among its respondents, 94% agreed there are plenty of clubs for
students to join and 94% agreed that many students participate. These figures rest on only 17 self-selected
responses, so they indicate broad satisfaction rather than a reliable participation rate, and should be read as
directional sentiment only. [Source: Niche — Charlotte Latin School]
Small-sample caveat applied deliberately: 17 responses cannot support a precise participation claim. No non-sport club participation
percentage is asserted anywhere in this document.
Context, Not a Substitute
For scale only: roughly 90% of Charlotte Latin students in grades 7–12 play at least one sanctioned sport. That is
an athletics figure and says nothing direct about club participation, but it establishes that co-curricular
engagement is a strong cultural norm at the School. Combined with the in-schedule club model, the reasonable
conclusion is that club participation is high and broad — without a publishable number to attach to it. [Source:
Wikipedia — Charlotte Latin School]
Source List
1. Charlotte Latin School — Student Clubs / Clubs (most-popular Middle School clubs; schedule model).
2. Niche — Charlotte Latin School, clubs & activities survey items (17 responses; accessed June 2026).
3. Wikipedia — Charlotte Latin School (athletics participation ~90%, grades 7–12).
4. Charlotte Latin School — Return-to-Campus schedule notes (activity/club period in the school day).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

---

sections.text:
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Service, Leadership & Civic Engagement
Research Area — Service clubs, student governance, and civic life
The largest non-sport, non-arts cluster: a Service Council slate culminating in the 150-hour Service Society, elected
Student and Honor Councils, the Hawks Lead leadership program, and affinity/advocacy clubs (Mosaic, SISTERS, Girl Up,
SADD).
AT A GLANCE
Coordinating body CLS Service Council organizes weekly service activities across the Upper
School.
Recognition Service Society honors students who accumulate 150+ service hours during
Upper School.
Documented volume The Class of 2018 reported 5,485 service hours by the end of junior year.
Federal recognition Students have earned the Presidential Volunteer Service Award (100+
hours/yr).
Governance bodies Elected Student Council and the Honor Council (with its Advisory Board).
Affinity & advocacy Mosaic (Q&A, BSA), SISTERS, Girl Up, SADD.
A Service-and-Leadership Culture
Service and leadership are woven through Charlotte Latin's stated mission — 'inspiring them to learn,
encouraging them to serve others' — and the club roster reflects it. This is the largest non-sport, non-arts cluster
by club count, structured around a coordinating Service Council, a formal recognition pathway (the Service
Society), and a set of leadership and affinity bodies. The School-wide leadership thread is branded Hawks Lead,
with dedicated leadership electives in the Upper School. [Sources: charlottelatin.org — Mission; Clubs; Hawks
Lead]
Service Clubs
Charlotte Latin runs a cluster of hands-on service clubs, most awarding service hours that count toward the
Service Society. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
Club Focus
Club Sandwich Makes sandwiches for people experiencing homelessness.
Blessings in a Backpack Weekly food-packing for students who lack weekend meals.
Paws for the Cause Blankets and toys for Humane Society shelter animals.
CLS Math Tutors Math tutoring partnerships with local schools.
Admissions Ambassadors Host and support prospective families at School events.
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Club Focus
Environmental Club Campus stream stewardship, recycling, Sierra Student Coalition.
The Service Society Pathway
Service at Charlotte Latin is not only club-based; the CLS Service Council organizes additional weekly service
opportunities, and students who accumulate more than 150 hours across their Upper School tenure are
recognized as members of the Charlotte Latin Service Society at graduation. The scale is real: the Class of
2018 reported 5,485 service hours by the end of junior year, and multiple students have earned the federal
Presidential Volunteer Service Award (which requires at least 100 hours in a calendar year). [Source:
charlottelatin.org — Upper School Profile]
Leadership & Governance Bodies
Student Council (StuCo)
The Student Council is made up of officers and delegates elected from each grade. Elections for rising grades
10–12 begin in the spring, while freshman officers and two delegates per grade are chosen in the fall. StuCo
brings student concerns to faculty and administration and plans campus events — the School's central
student-governance body. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
Honor Council & Honor Council Advisory Board
Charlotte Latin's culture is anchored by a student-supported Honor Code ('Honor Above All'). The elected Honor
Council administers it, and the Honor Council Advisory Board supports the Council by planning ceremonies
and assemblies and serving as a liaison across divisions. [Sources: charlottelatin.org — Clubs; Core Values]
Hawks Lead & leadership electives
Beyond clubs, leadership is taught: the Hawks Lead program runs across divisions, and the Upper School offers
three leadership electives in which students examine their own values, decision-making styles, and the
responsibilities of influence. This gives the leadership pathway a curricular spine, not just extracurricular bodies.
[Source: charlottelatin.org — Upper School; Hawks Lead]
Affinity, Identity & Advocacy
A set of clubs builds community and advocates for inclusion. Mosaic is the umbrella for diversity programming
and houses Q&A and the Black Student Association (BSA), working to celebrate cultural, religious, ethnic,
social, and racial diversity. SISTERS pairs upper-class women with freshmen women to ease the high-school
transition; Girl Up empowers women through education, advocacy, and service; and SADD raises awareness of
the dangers of impaired driving. [Source: charlottelatin.org — Clubs]
Civic-Engagement Read
The civic dimension at Charlotte Latin runs on two tracks that reinforce each other: a governance track (Student
Council, Honor Council, Hawks Lead) that gives students real responsibility inside the institution, and a
public-issues track (Speech & Debate, Model UN, World Quest, SADD, Girl Up) that turns them outward toward
policy and advocacy. The pairing is what makes the civic pathway the School's strongest non-arts identity —
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
covered competitively in the Academic & Competitive Programs dossier.

Volunteer Service Award).

sections.text:
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Thematic Pathways
Research Area — What clusters of clubs expose students to, and how
Charlotte Latin's clubs map onto five pathways: civic/public-voice (its deepest), global & cultural, STEM & innovation, a
narrower entrepreneurship thread, and a large service slate. Framed as exposure and demonstrated interest, not outcome
promises.
AT A GLANCE
Civic & Political Speech & Debate, Model UN, World Quest, Student Council, Honor Council —
argument, policy, governance, and public speaking.
Global & Cultural Model UN, World Quest, Spanish Club, Table Française, NJCL, plus the
Global Studies sister-school travel program.
STEM & Innovation Science Olympiad, Robotics, Math Club/Team, Environmental Club, anchored
by the MIT-affiliated Fab Lab.
Entrepreneurship Fab Lab prototyping plus the senior Entrepreneurship & Global Marketplace
Leadership elective; a thinner but real thread.
Service & Leadership The Service Council slate, Blessings in a Backpack, Club Sandwich, Paws for
the Cause, Girl Up, SADD — detailed in a companion dossier.
How Clubs Cluster Into Pathways
Individually, a club is a weekly meeting. Grouped, clubs form pathways — sets of activities that, taken together,
build toward a recognizable interest area or post-secondary direction. This dossier maps Charlotte Latin's
non-sport, non-arts clubs into five pathways and explains the mechanism: what a cluster exposes students to and
how. The framing is descriptive of exposure and demonstrated interest, not a promise of any outcome (e.g.,
admission or a career).
Pathway 1 — Civic, Political & Public-Voice
This is Charlotte Latin's deepest non-arts pathway. Speech & Debate (a top-20 national program) and its feeder
Forensics Club build argument, evidence, and public-speaking skill; Model United Nations applies those skills
to diplomacy and policy; World Quest tests current-affairs and geopolitical knowledge against other schools.
Governance experience comes from the elected Student Council and the Honor Council Advisory Board. A
student who strings these together gets sustained exposure to exactly the skills that surface in law, government,
journalism, and policy — reasoning under pressure, structured argument, and public deliberation. [Sources:
charlottelatin.org; NSDA]
Pathway 2 — Global & Cultural Exposure
Several clubs point outward to the wider world. Model UN attends conferences including the North American
Invitational Model UN at Georgetown, and the School notes that its Model UN and Debate programs have made
international trips. Language and culture clubs — Spanish Club, Table Française, and the National Junior
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE LATIN SCHOOL HAWKS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Classical League (Greek and Roman antiquity) — deepen cultural fluency, while World Quest builds global
literacy. These clubs sit alongside the School's Global Studies program, whose long-standing sister-school
relationships include schools in Germany (since 1989) and South Africa (since 2008), giving the cluster a
genuine travel and exchange dimension. [Sources: charlottelatin.org — Global Studies; Upper School Profile]
Pathway 3 — STEM & Innovation
The STEM cluster is anchored by the Fab Lab, an official outgrowth of MIT's Center for Bits and Atoms,
equipped with 3D printers, laser cutters, CNC machines, and digital-design software. Around it sit competitive
and exploratory clubs: Science Olympiad (Division B in Middle School, Division C in Upper School), Robotics,
the Math Club / CLS Math Team, and the Environmental Club with its campus stream-stewardship work. The
pathway exposes students to engineering design, hands-on prototyping, applied science competition, and
computational thinking. A well-known proof point: a student-led Fab Lab campaign produced 3D-printed and
injection-molded face shields for medical workers during the early COVID-19 pandemic. [Sources:
charlottelatin.org; Wikipedia]
Pathway 4 — Entrepreneurship
Entrepreneurship is a real but narrower thread, carried more by coursework and the Fab Lab than by a dedicated
club. The senior elective Entrepreneurship & Global Marketplace Leadership offers a project-based,
multidisciplinary approach to creative problem-solving, and the Fab Lab gives students a place to prototype
product ideas. There is no standalone DECA/FBLA-style business-competition club evident in the School's
published club list — flagged here so the pathway is not overstated. [Sources: charlottelatin.org — Upper School
Profile; Innovation & Design]
Honest limit: this pathway leans on a course plus the Fab Lab rather than a club. If a business or entrepreneurship club exists
term-to-term, it is not in the School's published roster.
Pathway 5 — Service & Leadership (Cross-Reference)
Charlotte Latin's largest cluster by sheer club count is service and leadership — the Service Council slate,
Blessings in a Backpack, Club Sandwich, Paws for the Cause, CLS Math Tutors, Girl Up, SADD, Admissions
Ambassadors, and the leadership bodies. Because it is so substantial, it is treated in its own dossier (Service,
Leadership & Civic Engagement) rather than compressed here.
Reading the Pathways Honestly
Two cautions. First, these clusters describe exposure: joining Model UN exposes a student to diplomacy and
research; it does not 'get them noticed' for anything by itself. Second, the strongest, most externally validated
pathways at Charlotte Latin are the civic/public-voice and STEM clusters, because they have national results and
dedicated facilities behind them. The global, entrepreneurship, and (within this dossier) service threads are real
but rest more on program structure than on competitive hardware.
Source List
1. Charlotte Latin School — Student Clubs / Clubs; Leading Programs (Global Studies, Innovation & Design).
2. Charlotte Latin School — Upper School Profile (Entrepreneurship & Global Marketplace Leadership; Fab Lab; international trips).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

sections.text:
# Charlotte Latin School — Student Clubs Redesign Deep Research

**Provenance.** Compiled 2026-07-26 by Claude Code for the Student Clubs sub-section
redesign (cards 1a Affinity & Identity Groups, 1b Service & Civic Engagement,
1c Honor Societies). Method: direct HTML reads of charlottelatin.org (the site is
Finalsite, has no `sitemap.xml`, and its search is JS-driven, so pages were scraped
directly rather than fetched by guessed slug), plus three Upper School Profile PDFs and
the Family Handbook PDF.

**Confidence key.** VERIFIED = read directly from a live page or PDF. NOT PUBLISHED =
explicitly searched and absent. REFUTED = the school's own pages contradict the premise.

**Headline.** Two research premises were **refuted** by the school's own live pages:
Charlotte Latin has **no service-hours graduation requirement**, and it publishes **no
affinity-group count or roster**, so there is no count discrepancy to flag. Honor-society
coverage is essentially one society.

---

sections.preview: ### The coordinating structure — VERIFIED The DEI page's student section is headed "Student Programs - Alliance Clubs": "The student-led Diversity Club and Alliance Groups align perfectly with our school's mission as they raise awareness about issues of inclusion of, respect for, and civility toward all persons across…
sections.text:
### The coordinating structure — VERIFIED

The DEI page's student section is headed **"Student Programs - Alliance Clubs"**:
"The student-led Diversity Club and Alliance Groups align perfectly with our school's
mission as they raise awareness about issues of inclusion of, respect for, and civility
toward all persons across many dimensions of identity." No founding year is published.
Named staff: **Vernette Rucker, Assistant Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion**.
→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/diversity-equity-inclusion

### The enumerable structure — VERIFIED

The only named identity group is a **club**, not a separate affinity page:

**Mosaic (Upper School)** — "To promote diversity in and outside of our school community
through events that celebrate our cultural, religious, ethnic, social and racial diversity.
We strive to promote inclusivity and respect for all kinds of human diversity through
appreciation and acceptance. **Under Mosaic we have Q&A and BSA.**"
→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/student-life/student-clubs/clubs

So the structure is **Mosaic** (umbrella club) → two sub-groups, **Q&A** and **BSA**. The
initialisms are **not expanded anywhere on the site** and must not be glossed.

Identity-adjacent Upper School clubs on the same roster:

- **Girl Up** — "To empower all women at CLS though education, advocacy, and service"
- **SISTERS** — freshman-women / upperclass-women mentoring pairs

### Faculty and parent structures — VERIFIED

**Divisional DEI Committees** (faculty/staff). For parents: **Parent DEI Education Learning
Sessions** and the **Parent Cookbook Club** — "transform the typical book club model into an
immersive cultural experience… exploring diverse cultures one delicious recipe at a time."
→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/diversity-equity-inclusion

### Gaps — 1a

- **No count of affinity groups is published anywhere**, so the anticipated "N advertised
 vs. N enumerated" discrepancy **does not exist** at this school. The DEI page HTML was
 checked directly, including collapsed accordion markup — the only occurrence of
 "affinity/alliance" is the single sentence quoted above. **No count flag is rendered.**
- **The "Diversity Club List" link is a dead end.** The DEI page links to `/fs/pages/2417`,
 which renders the same generic sentence and **contains no list**. →
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/fs/pages/2417
- **No Lower/Middle School affinity groups** published; no per-division breakout.
- **No parent affinity groups** — the Cookbook Club is parent DEI programming, not an
 identity-based affinity group.
- **No student diversity leadership corps and no NAIS SDLC mention** anywhere reachable,
 including https://www.charlottelatin.org/leading-programs/student-leadership-development

### REFUTED — a cross-school attribution error, do not ingest

An early search snippet attributed programs called **"Voices – Brotherhood & Identity"
(Grades 3–5)** and **"The Boys' Room" (Middle School)**, plus "affinity programming for
historically underrepresented boys in Grades 3–12," to Charlotte Latin. **None of it could
be verified** — those strings appear nowhere in the live DEI page HTML, and a targeted
search returned no Charlotte Latin source. Almost certainly another school's programming.
**Excluded.**

---

sections.preview: ### REFUTED — there is no service-hours graduation requirement The school states verbatim: "Latin does not have a formal requirement of service hours for graduation. We believe that our students find meaningful ways to engage in the community through our school-based partnerships and their familial-based…
sections.text:
### REFUTED — there is no service-hours graduation requirement

The school states verbatim: **"Latin does not have a formal requirement of service hours
for graduation. We believe that our students find meaningful ways to engage in the community
through our school-based partnerships and their familial-based organizations."**
→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/leading-programs/student-leadership-development/service

Corroborated twice: the Upper School Profile — "Although service is not required, students
design, manage, and staff a wide variety of on-going weekly programs"
(https://www.charlottelatin.org/uploaded/COMPOSER/AcademicsTab/USprofile1718.pdf) — and the
Family Handbook: "Service is not a graduation requirement."
(https://www.charlottelatin.org/uploaded/COMPOSER/PortalUploads/All_School/CLSfamilyhandbook1819.pdf)

**URL note:** the working service page is
`/leading-programs/student-leadership-development/service`. The commonly cited
`/programs/service` returns **HTTP 404**.

### Program 1 — Latin Service Society — scale: 150 hours, founded 1997-98

A **recognition** program, not a requirement: "Latin's Service Society encourages Upper
School students to participate in various Community-Engaged Learning experiences and
recognizes students who make significant contributions to the community through service,"
using a reflection-based model across all four Upper School years.

Family Handbook: "To be inducted into the Service Society, a four-year student must perform
**150 hours** of service," prorated for transfers; and "The level of student involvement in
the Service Program since the Service Society's formation during the **1997-1998** school
year has been gratifying."

- Sources: https://www.charlottelatin.org/leading-programs/student-leadership-development/service ·
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/uploaded/COMPOSER/PortalUploads/All_School/CLSfamilyhandbook1819.pdf

### Program 2 — Habitat for Humanity — scale: four houses, and a national first

"Charlotte Latin is the **first private or independent school in the country** with a senior
class that funded and built a Habitat for Humanity House," and "The Latin community has
funded and built **four Habitat houses** and regularly assists with Habitat builds both
locally and in El Salvador."
→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/leading-programs/student-leadership-development/service

### Program 3 — Community Partners & Principles of Good Practice — scale: 3 school-wide partners, 6 principles

Named school-wide partners: **Baby Bundles**, **Special Olympics**, **Habitat for Humanity
of the Charlotte Region**. The six Principles of Good Practice for Community-Engaged
Learning: Sustained Partnerships · Safety · Reciprocity + Interrelatedness · Consistent
Communication · Humility + Dignity · Training + Reflection (the site renders the last as the
typo "Reflextion"). A fourth initiative, **Good Neighbors**, provides campus gym space to
community organizations.
→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/leading-programs/student-leadership-development/service

### Additional verified scale figures

- **3,396 community service hours** by the Class of 2023 by the end of junior year —
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/uploaded/Veracross/Upper_School_Profile_for_Admissions.pdf
- **5,485 hours** by the Class of 2018 by the end of junior year, with **five** class members
 qualifying for the Service Society; **seven** students earned a **Presidential Volunteer
 Service Award** in 2016-17 (requires 100+ hours in a calendar year) —
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/uploaded/COMPOSER/AcademicsTab/USprofile1718.pdf
- The **Upper School Service Council** organizes "numerous service-related activities…
 available to students each and every week"; the 150-hour Service Society recognition is
 conferred at the end of senior year —
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/student-life/student-clubs/clubs

### "Individual activity, not a club" — VERIFIED

From the clubs page's **"SPECIAL NOTES"** section, listed *separately from* the club roster:

- **Blessings in a Backpack** — "meets every Wednesday during the year to pack non-perishable
 foods… distributed to students who receive free lunch and breakfast at their school but may
 not have access to food over the weekend" — a standing activity, not an enumerated club.
- **StuCo / Student Council** — elected officers and delegates, not open-enrollment.
- **CLS Service Council**-organized weekly activities — individual service activity rather
 than club membership.

→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/student-life/student-clubs/clubs

---

Fox Chapter | Upper School | Top academic achievement; honors "the ideals exemplified by the Greek words Areté (excellence), Diké…
sections.text:
### The roster — VERIFIED (three, and only one is a conventional academic society)

| Society | Division | What it recognizes | Feeds from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cum Laude Society — Edward J. Fox Chapter** | Upper School | Top academic achievement; honors "the ideals exemplified by the Greek words Areté (excellence), Diké (justice), and Timé (honor)" | The classroom |
| **Latin Service Society** | Upper School | Significant contribution to the community through service; 150 hours | Service |
| **International Thespian Society** | Upper School | "To honor excellence in high school theater; a part of the Educational Theatre Association" (listed as a *club*) | The Arts — theatre |

### Cum Laude detail — unusually well documented for this set

- Society founded **1906**; Latin's chapter chartered **1976**, when the school was six years
 old — "making Latin the youngest school ever so recognized."
- **Annual induction count IS published: 28 new members** (14 from the Class of '25 and 14
 from the Class of '24). Head of School Chuck Baldecchi: "It's a tribute to the school's
 long-standing regard for academic excellence."
- → https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/school-news/news-details/~board/news/post/charlotte-latin-students-inducted-into-cum-laude-society
- **Induction criteria ARE published** — in the Family Handbook rather than on the news page:
 "Induction into the Cum Laude Society is the highest academic honor a student can receive
 at Charlotte Latin School… **Seniors in the top 20% of their class and juniors in the top
 10%** of their class who have completed at least two full semesters at the School are
 eligible for induction," with additional requirements for "intellectual curiosity and
 character," and "As mandated by the national organization, no one with an honor violation
 record may be admitted into the society."
 → https://www.charlottelatin.org/uploaded/COMPOSER/PortalUploads/All_School/CLSfamilyhandbook1819.pdf

This makes Charlotte Latin the **only school in the comparison set that publishes both
induction criteria and an induction count** — so its 1c card carries no gap flag on those
two points.

### Related non-society academic honors — VERIFIED (label accordingly)

**Headmaster's List** (GPA 3.50+, no grade below C−) and **Junior Marshals** (juniors in the
top 10% by cumulative average through the first semester of junior year, who assist at
Commencement).
→ https://www.charlottelatin.org/uploaded/COMPOSER/PortalUploads/All_School/CLSfamilyhandbook1819.pdf

### NOT FOUND — explicitly searched

The live club roster, the DEI page, the Student Leadership page, the 2025 Honors and Awards
Ceremony article, the Family Handbook PDF, and three Upper School Profile PDFs were all
checked. **No published evidence of:** National Honor Society, National Junior Honor
Society, National Art Honor Society, Tri-M Music Honor Society, Quill & Scroll, Rho Kappa,
Mu Alpha Theta, Science National Honor Society, National Latin Honor Society, or any
French/Spanish/Chinese world-language honor society. A keyword scan of the Family Handbook
returned **zero hits** for every one of those names.

Two nuances that explain the absence:

- **Subject-area and world-language recognition at Latin is delivered as named prizes, not
 honor societies** — the Victor Hugo Award (French), Homer Award (Greek), Petrarch Award
 (Latin), Cervantes Award (Spanish), Bausch + Lomb Honorary Science Award, and Rensselaer
 Medal. The 2025 Honors and Awards Ceremony article is exhaustive and names **no honor
 society at all**, which is strong negative evidence. →
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/school-news/news-details/~board/news/post/2025-honors-and-awards-ceremony
- **The closest classics analogue is a club, not a society:** the **National Junior Classical
 League** — "To encourage an interest in and an appreciation of the language, literature,
 and culture of ancient Greece and Rome…" →
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/student-life/student-clubs/clubs

### Gaps — 1c

- **No Middle School honor society** is published. The Middle School club model is
 rotational rather than honorary: "Middle School students choose a club from more than 25
 offerings. Students meet with their clubs once a week for a period of 8-10 weeks, and then
 try a different club." **No Middle School clubs are individually named** on the site beyond
 examples (Cooking Club, Just Dance Club, Robotics Club, Student Council, Sports Club).
- Apart from the single Cum Laude induction article, **no chapter activity** is published for
 any society.

---
